processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The Fe–15Mn–9Al-0.9C–5Ni (15Mn5Ni) low-density steel grade was prepared by vacuum induction melting; the sound portion of the 30 kg ingot was used.
Homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h before hot rolling.
Hot rolled at 1323 K to a final plate thickness of ~13 mm; this processing condition is referred to as HR. Details of the hot rolling process were reported elsewhere [21].

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled (HR) condition: equiaxed, near-randomly textured γ (austenite) matrix (d ~5–7 μm) containing B2 phase in the form of elongated bamboo-like stringers and polygonal particles, together with κ-carbides; a two/three-phase γ + B2 (+ κ-carbide) microstructure. 15Mn5Ni contained a higher B2 fraction (~12%) and higher κ-carbide volume fraction than the 28Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni alloys, and a lower twin fraction than the higher-Mn alloys.

microstructure_list.region: within γ matrix (stringers and polygonal particles)

phases_present.morphology: elongated stringers (bamboo-like morphology) and polygonal particles

precipitates.type: B2 phase (elongated bamboo-like stringers and polygonal particles)

interfaces.interface_notes: In the HR condition B2 exists as elongated bamboo-like stringers and polygonal particles within the γ matrix. b0073 notes that recrystallized grains nucleate mostly along γ/γ boundaries and the γ/B2 interface (during subsequent heat treatment of the cold-rolled material). No interface coherency/character data are reported specifically for the HR condition.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s; hardness averaged over ten measurements on each sample

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Per ASTM E−140-02; hardness averaged over ten measurements on each sample
characterization_methods.purpose: To evaluate hardness change with cold work and heat treatment of the alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: Initial HR-condition hardness of the 15Mn5Ni alloy was ~375 ± 6 VHN.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-SEM equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors (Oxford); TSL-OIM software; step sizes 120 nm and 250 nm over ~100×100 μm² / ~200×200 μm² areas
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples polished to colloidal silica ~100 nm finish; three scans per sample; KAM and GOS (2°) criteria used; Σ3 CSL boundaries used to compute twin fraction
characterization_methods.purpose: To characterize grain orientations, grain size, twin fractions, phase contrast and recrystallization of austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: HR microstructures of all three alloys were reported in a previous study [21] and used as the starting condition.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument, Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification (γ, B2, κ-carbide) in cold-rolled and heat-treated conditions
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to track B2 and κ-carbide formation/dissolution with heat treatment; HR was the starting condition prior to cold rolling.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI TECNAI 20T G2 TEM operating at 200 kV equipped with EDAX EDS; twin-jet electropolishing at 243 K (-30 °C)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Bright-field and dark-field imaging; dark-field captured from (010) κ satellite spot
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify phases (κ-carbides and B2 particles) and finer microstructural features not resolvable by SEM-EBSD
characterization_methods.key_findings: B2 identified as FeAl-based phase containing Mn and Ni; intragranular and intergranular B2 and κ-carbides characterized in heat-treated samples.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Post-tensile fracture surface examination of failed specimens
characterization_methods.purpose: To examine fracture mode of tensile specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Mn5Ni tensile specimens heat treated at low temperature failed by quasi-cleavage/intergranular cracking along γ/B2 interphase boundaries.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Walter+Bai AG testing machine; flat specimens gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm/min (initial strain rate ~3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹), per ASTM E8M; triplicated for each condition
characterization_methods.purpose: To evaluate strength and ductility of the alloys in different processing conditions
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to obtain YS, UTS and total elongation; HR-condition ductility of the alloys ranged ~20–70% with 15Mn5Ni lowest.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 15Mn5Ni alloy (Table 1, wt.%, balance Fe): Mn 14.7 ± 0.3, Al 9.8 ± 0.05, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni 4.1 ± 0.05.

The 15Mn5Ni alloy in the HR condition contained a higher B2 fraction (~12%) than 28Mn5Ni (~4%), and the alloy composition series was designed to give a B2 fraction varying from 0 to ~12% in the hot-rolled condition.

In the HR condition the three LDS alloys exhibited about 20–70% total tensile elongation to failure at room temperature (from prior study [21]), with the 15Mn5Ni alloy displaying the lowest ductility; this suggested an increased tendency for cracking when cold rolling exceeds 50% reduction.
The 15Mn5Ni alloy experienced cracking beyond 50% cold reduction; hence cold rolling was restricted to ~50% reduction for all alloys for comparison.

The hot-rolled microstructures of all three alloys (including 15Mn5Ni) were reported in a previous study [21] and serve as the starting condition for the cold rolling study; the present paper's detailed EBSD/XRD/TEM characterization focuses on the HR+CR and heat-treated conditions.
